tips.comment: Won over this trip at Chelmsford when last seen in March 2025 under today's jockey and should improve for that run on the back of an absence of 186 days.

Jumbeau is returning to the turf after a spell racing on the all weather.She is much better on grass .She has ran well in better races than this on firmish ground and is on a good mark especiallt with Jack callans 7lb claim.

Trinity College is a 3-year-old son of Dubawi ex Hermosa, who herself is a dual 1,000 Guineas winner and from the family of Hydrangea by Galileo. He runs here in this Listed race over 1m2f off a mark of 105. He won his 1m maiden at 10/11f at Galway by 12 lengths last September. Last time out, he won his 1m race at 10/11f at Naas in March. He'll now be ridden by R.L. Moore for Aidan O'Brien and Coolmore. Drawn 4/7 here, I think if he can break and make the rails position, he can make all for some Black Type.

Won over the distance last time out at Chelmsford. The form of that race has worked out well. Stable going well, should be hard to beat today. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable has won this race eight times.

Has won on GF and won at Goodwood last season, showing he can handle an undulating track. Won well last time on his reappearance run and should confirm form with those who finished behind him that day, with him expected to come on for the run.

Beaten a neck over this trip by the re-opposing City Of Delight at Doncaster last time out, but is better off in the weights to reverse that form. It should be more suited to the uphill finish, being a former winner over further.

Solid performer who picked up a couple of wins last season and reappeared with a decent 5th beaten less than 2 lengths at Doncaster last month. Reopposes with a number of those rivals today but appears more favoured by the weights so should run well.

Sean has been racing in Meydan and then came back and ran down the field at Doncaster, but that was on good/soft ground, which is not what this one wants. Back on firm ground and on a tight track should bring out the best.
Two wins here at Epsom back in September, and a couple more since then in last four races. Good chance now running back at one mile four furlongs.
Hollie Doyle booked and interesting at the foot of the weights after being gelded over winter. Unexposed at this trip and won here last year over 10f from 3 lbs lower on decent ground.
Third of seven over this trip at Brighton 10 days ago and will come on for that run following an absence of 173 days.
Decent near two length win at Southwell after returning from a 137-day break and a gelding op. Should do well here if transferring all-weather form across here to turf for the first time.
Convincing win last time out at Brighton by over three lengths and should continue that here with a small rise. Favourable high draw here.

Orbaan may be 10 years old, but he is on a very low weight, 10 lbs below a win at Carlisle less than 12 months ago on firmish ground. He has won at Epsom in the past. This may be his swansong. They have kept him going, and he will be ready if he has anything left after 68 runs and 6 wins.

Has won five times in this grade, so has been astutely placed. Top rider Hollie Doyle in the pigskin, and she has won on him twice from three rides. Four wins in these underfoot conditions and is a course and distance winner too. Fresh record not that flash, but maybe he can turn it around this time?
His best run came over this trip and Darragh Keenan was also riding him that day. Has been dropped in the weights since then so should be good enough to win this.

Thrice raced maiden who hasn't made much of an impact in his trio of starts to date however after a 173 day break having been gelded in the process of that break and now stepping up significantly in trip going over 1 mile 2 furlongs for the first time that being a wise move by his connections as this new trip can unlock a whole a new level of improvement also making his handicap debut of a reasonable mark of 67 this gelded son of Wootton Bassett & Safina ( Dam's sire Pivotal ) can be a whole different proposition on this return and this looks like another one of trainer Sir Mark Prescott's interesting looking projects he does very well with where he usually gives them a trio of quick novice runs and then patiently gives them time to mature once they have been properly accessed and rated he then steps them up in trip and trainer Sir Mark Prescott has his horses in top nick fit and ready to go and Requiem is certainly one that needs considering in a suitable looking return assignment with jockey Luke Morris taking the ride

The trainer does really well with his handicap debutantes and it's very interesting that he has such a good record at this course. It looks very much like a plot job now that the horse is being sent handicapping and taking a big step up in trip. His runners have started to perform better in the last week or two and I'm expecting the horse to step up on previous efforts here as they so often do for this yard off generous looking handicap marks.

Went third close to home but no extra inside the final half a furlong over this trip on the Lingfield Polytrack on the first of this month and should come on for that run following an absence of 161 days. The first-time visor could fire up too.

The model I run suggests Fiver Friday can win this race ahead of Double Digits in second and Evaluation in third. This result has largely been driven by Fiver Friday having the significantly larger RPR of the field. Sets out carrying the least weight out of the rest of the top of the market, and with the jockey on board also claiming 5 lbs, looks set to get over the line first. Good form having run first at Naas in a field of 20 runners over the same 2m distance.

The model I run simulates this race and has Far Away West coming first. Admittedly this simulated result looks a bit out of line, so maybe an each way play here offers some room for error and retains value bet characteristics, particularly when 4 places are on offer. Pete Kavanagh on board is claiming 3 lbs, whilst this horse is already carrying the second lowest weight of the 14 runner field. This horse does actually have the highest RPR of the field.

The model I run simulates this race and has Low Mileage coming in first ahead of Pure Surf in second and Toombridge in third. Edward Austin on board is claiming 5 lbs, which brings the weights more in line to the top of the market, and Low Mileage has the second highest RPR of the field.
In great form, having won three of her last four races. Last win was over course and distance in a sixteen-horse race, and she will appreciate this drop in class.
Looks on a handy weight here. Has not won since 2023 but showed nice form last time when fifth at Wetherby in first-time cheekpieces. Also has course and winner form, which is a bonus.

Super Citizen franked some very consistent lead-up form by winning stoutly last time out, and a repeat looks on the cards with B Hughes in the saddle for a very good yard. Course and distance winner, so that augurs well. Ready to go on with it now.

Harlem Nights is one serious contender now returning to a turf track with ground conditions spot on for him and this race should also suit his nature of going perfectly well given the horses enrolled to run here Jessica Macey's Dark Angel gelding was last seen at Wolverhampton 22 days ago where finishing a reasonable 4th/7 his mark continues to ease and is now operating on a mark of 66 that being a total of 8lb below his last winning mark and seeing he ticks every box here he must be taken extremely seriously especially now he is off the handicappers radar and it would be a wise and profitable move to catch him running well at this stage while off the handicappers rader jockey Lewis Edmunds takes the ride and can give Harlem Nights the perfect ride here at Thirsk . Respected .

Well supported on seasonal debut at Musselburgh 9 days ago but lost many lengths at the start and was allowed to come home in his own time. Remains on the same mark and could go close if breaking smarter.
Kept on well when runner-up over the extended mile at Newcastle 12 days ago and could appreciate this drop in trip.

This horse won on his penultimate start where the front two pulled away, and the runner-up then won his next race. That suggests he should be competitive off this 2lb higher mark. The horse didn't perform at Newcastle last time out, but I'm happy to ignore that effort since he'd also not performed there in his previous three visits to the track. His second of 15 on fast ground at Redcar last year was off just a 1lb lower mark and showed that he isn't just an AW horse, but can perform well on turf when it's riding quick.

A poor basement handicap where 12/1 shot Without Delay appeals. He ran well at Musselburgh on his seasonal reappearance 3 weeks ago off a higher mark, and with a fast pace up top, he should be able to outstay his rivals late on.

The model I run suggests Pooroldmackley can win this one ahead of Mr. Zee in second and Bradman in third. This result has largely been driven by Pooroldmackley having the best RPR of the field. He does step out with the joint lowest Or here, meaning he has a nice weight margin of 21 lbs to the top of the market. Evan Williams has a high RTF % and Pooroldmackley comes here in good form after a solid 3rd here at this track for 2m before going on to make all 2 days ago at Newton Abbot for 2m 3f in the same size field.

The model I run suggests Military Alliance can win this one ahead of God Of Fire in second and Jackstell in third. Military Alliance has the highest RPR of the field and the joint highest Official Rating. This, combined with the racecard all having the same weight, means it will be down to horse/jockey/trainer ability. This horse is an ex-Irish, and I fancy this as the value bet with Paul O'Brien picking up the reins.

The model I run suggests Atlanta Brave should win this race. Atlanta Brave has the highest RPR of the field and has a similar official rating to A Definite Getaway and Comino Rocio. James Bowen on board is in good form.

Won over C&D 3 starts back on better ground and followed up that win with another win at Leicester before a good 2nd to Pep Talking LTO, who franked the form by winning again next time out. Same mark here in a very winnable race.
Twice a winner over fences and once rated as high as 113. His mark has slipped to just 88 which looks tempting and is a previous winner here.

Has a course and distance win off a similar handicap mark to this. His last race, where I thought he wasn't ridden to advantage, has produced six individual winners from it. The trainer had a winner the other day, so all in all, he looks a fair each-way bet.
Really hasn't been disgraced of late in class 2 company and he has to be respected dropping into class 4 company off a winnable rating.
Got some decent Class 2 Handicap Hurdle form in the book, and he has to be of strong interest dropping in class.

The model I run suggests Plantaroma can win this one. Lots of placings recently and can get over the line first here. Plantaroma has the second highest RPR of the field, but the lowest OR means a huge weight advantage over the 2m trip.

Magic Seven was wisely put aside after failing miserably at Cheltenham in December and resumes here off the back of a 190-day spell. Won first-up in 2023 and it's not beyond the realms of possibility he could repeat that here with the same jockey.

The model I run suggests Race To Base can win this one ahead of Emerald Time in second and Le Docteur in third. Sam Twiston-Davies picks up the reins. Race To Base has the best form on offer here and has the previous history of running the course and distance.
